_comment: Asha declarative PreToolUse policy rules. Evaluated by hooks/handlers/policy-guard.sh. User overrides/additions: ~/.asha/policies.json (merged by id, user wins). Schema per rule: {id, tool (anchored ERE on tool_name), command_regex|file_path_regex (ERE matched against the Bash command / file path), action: deny|ask|warn (warn = log-only via violation-checker, never blocks), command_regex|file_path_regex, exclude_regex? (ERE; suppresses a matched rule when the command/path ALSO matches it — e.g. 'Memory/ but NOT the mutable subset'), reason, override_env?}. NOTE: this is a soft string-pattern DETERRENT, not containment — command_regex matches short -r/-R only (long flags like --recursive and indirection like 'cd /home && find .' slip through), and an agent can evade deliberately. Pair with the harness's own permission/sandbox controls for hard limits.

rules._comment: v3 after the 2026-08-04 adversarial review: targets now include ~, $HOME, quoted and doubled-slash forms (the most natural accidental phrasings all bypassed v2 — grep -r pattern ~ was ALLOWED); grep arm tolerates flags before the recursive flag (--include=*.md -R); [^|;&] stops the tool arm crossing && into an unrelated path (v2 denied 'find ./src -name x && cd /home/alice'). Scoped forms (~/Code, $HOME/Code, /home/user/dir) stay allowed. Known residual: an expanded-at-runtime variable other than $HOME still passes — the guard sees the unexpanded string.
rules.reason: Blocked broad scan over /home — unscoped find/grep/bfs/fd/rg across a whole home directory causes severe disk pressure, badly so on rotational storage or alongside a background sync client (Asha learning no-broad-home-scans, conf 0.95). Scope to a subdirectory, or set ASHA_ALLOW_BROAD_SCAN=1 to allow. Tune or remove this rule in ~/.asha/policies.json if it does not fit your machine.

Blocked destructive git operation — irreversible, or affects shared state. Discarding uncommitted work (checkout --, restore, clean -f) has no reflog: use `git stash` instead, which is recoverable. Force-push: use --force-with-lease, which is permitted. History rewrites (filter-repo, filter-branch) invalidate every existing clone and cannot be undone once pushed — re-verify the blast radius, and prefer a fresh repo over rewriting a shared one. Set ASHA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_GIT=1 to allow.

Blocked rm of an archive or shell glob. Deleting an archive before its contents are extracted AND verified is the incident class this rule exists for — extract first, confirm the files are readable, then remove, or move to `.trash/` instead. This arm deliberately has NO path exemptions (not even /tmp/): an archive is unextracted data wherever it sits, and a path exemption anywhere in the command previously suppressed protection for every other target on the same line. Set ASHA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DELETE=1 to allow.
rules._comment: MUST stay ordered before destructive-delete: first match wins, and this rule's empty path-exemption budget is the mixed-target fix from the 2026-08-04 adversarial review ('rm -rf /tmp/extract pdfs.7z' was ALLOWED because /tmp/ matched the general rule's exclude anywhere in the command). The ["']? before the terminator covers quoted filenames ('rm "backup.7z"' previously slipped through).

rules.reason: Blocked irreversible deletion (rm -r/-f, shred, gh repo delete). Prefer moving to a `.trash/` staging dir over deleting outright. Regenerable trees (node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, /tmp), package/container removal (git rm, npm rm, docker rm), and Asha's own Work/markers/ files are exempt. Set ASHA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DELETE=1 to allow.
rules._comment: Reworked after the 2026-08-04 adversarial review. Path exemptions are now scoped to the rm segment itself (rm[[:space:]]["']?[^|;&]*(...)) — previously '/tmp/' ANYWHERE in the command suppressed the rule, so 'rm -rf important && mkdir -p /tmp/stage' was ALLOWED. Work/markers/ exemption fixes the review's BLOCKER: /rp:end, /rp:start, /session:silence and /session:restore all instruct 'rm -f Work/markers/<x>' and were denied by v1 — a guard that blocks its own toolkit's shipped cleanup gets overridden into uselessness. Known residual, accepted: a manager-prefix in a LATER segment ('rm -rf x; git rm y') still suppresses, because ERE cannot tie that exclusion to the segment that matched; and mixed targets inside ONE rm where an exempt path sits beside a precious NON-ARCHIVE target ('rm -rf /tmp/a precious-dir') are still suppressed — the archive rule above removes the worst class. This is a string-pattern deterrent, not containment (see file _comment).

rules.reason: Blocked edit to an immutable Memory/ file (identity/config). Mutable files (sessions/, activeContext, techEnvironment, workflowProtocols, scratchpad, ideas, vector_db) are exempt. Set ASHA_ALLOW_MEMORY_EDIT=1 to allow.

File written into a content root (Vault/Lore/Wiki/Codex/Compendium/Archive) outside its expected top-level buckets (World/Books/Sessions/Characters/Templates/Resources). Warn-only: this is a scatter check, not a block.
rules._comment: The content root must stay a NAMED anchor, not a wildcard. It is what scopes the rule: with a wildcard root the trigger degenerates to 'every write not in a bucket', which measured 129/129 markdown files in this repo — CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, every doc. The root list is the portable part and is meant to be extended; the taxonomy is the project-specific part. A project whose content lives elsewhere (docs/setting/, notes/) redefines this whole row in ~/.asha/policies.json, merged by id. Warn-only by design: violation-checker logs it, the guard never blocks, so a wrong root list costs a log line rather than a failed write.
